declarations.statement: In this paper, we introduce bGPT, a model designed for binary data processing and digital world modelling by next byte prediction.

display.title: bGPT: next byte prediction model for digital world simulation
display.summary: Introduces bGPT, a model trained via next byte prediction on native binary data to process digital media and simulate digital systems, treating all data types as byte sequences in a single framework.

declarations.statement: We start by present- ing its hierarchical Transformer framework, which segments byte sequences into patches to manage computational effi- ciency. Subsequently, we present the training objectives of bGPT, including generative modelling and classification.

display.title: Hierarchical patch-based byte Transformer with generative and classification objectives
display.summary: bGPT segments byte sequences into fixed-size patches, using a linear projection, patch-level decoder and byte-level decoder, trained with next byte prediction and then adapted to classification via pooled features.

declarations.statement: Our experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of bGPT in modelling digital media data, which showcases modality-agnostic knowledge transfer.

display.title: Byte-level digital media modelling with cross-modal knowledge transfer
display.summary: bGPT performs generative modelling and classification on text, audio and images at the byte level without modality-specific design, approaching specialized models and showing modality-agnostic knowledge transfer.

display.title: Algorithm simulation via ABC-MIDI symbolic music conversion
display.summary: bGPT learns to simulate and reverse-engineer conversion between text-based ABC notation and binary MIDI files, reaching 0.0011 bits per byte for ABC-to-MIDI conversion.

display.summary: Introduces a 2.1-million-instance dataset pairing machine-instruction memory blocks with sequences of 16-byte CPU register states for a simplified CPU.

originality.reasoning: The paper itself reports MegaByte as a multi-modal byte model and says bGPT adapts its hierarchical patch architecture; the stated distinction is application scope (native binary data, simulation), not modelling. The originality therefore rests on tasks/evaluation, which the framing ('paradigm shift', 'introduce bGPT') does not make explicit. Cited works' content is author-reported and not independently verified.
points: Authors position bGPT as next-byte prediction for native binary data, but their own background concedes prior byte models (ByteFormer, MegaByte, MambaByte) already model bytes across modalities; the architectural difference from MegaByte is not stated.

claim_support.reasoning: Byte-wise accuracy counts every byte of each 16-byte state, and many of those bytes may simply be copied from the previous state. Without a copy-previous-state baseline, the 99.99% figure may overstate how well the model simulates the CPU. Byte-wise accuracy includes many trivially copied bytes (unchanged registers); without a copy-previous-state baseline or held-out instruction compositions, 99.99% and emergence cannot be interpreted.
points: The CPU-simulation claim lacks simple baselines, and byte-wise accuracy may be inflated by bytes that are easy to predict.
CPU and conversion results lack any baseline; 'beyond memorization' and 'emergent ability' are not tested.

significance.reasoning: The reported table values show very low BPB for ABC→MIDI conversion and very high byte accuracy for CPU state prediction.
points: Simulating CPU state updates and ABC→MIDI conversion with a single byte model is a fresh and potentially impactful demonstration.

author_originality_statements.statement: Inspired by the success of next token prediction in natural lan- guage processing, we introduce bGPT, a model with next byte prediction to simulate the digi- tal world. bGPT matches specialized models in performance across various modalities, including text, audio, and images, and offers new possibil- ities for predicting, simulating, and diagnosing algorithm or hardware behaviour.
